Hi Sanjay / Maya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciated the deep dive on your use case and constraints. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can align with your security and networking teams: 

Summary of call:
- Goal: Host LLM inference for patient-facing triage flows behind ACME Health's private VPC.
- Major constraints: no egress of PII outside customer-controlled network, tenant isolation, strong logging controls for audit, and the option to run in an on-prem/air-gapped environment if required.

Follow-ups / items we promised to deliver:
1) Dataflow diagram showing where inference executes, where token-level data flows, and egress boundaries (attached: acmehealth-dataflow-diagram.png).
2) SOC2 Type II and SOC report stub for our hosted control plane (attached: SOC2-Type2-Redwood.pdf).
3) Short note on logging/retention defaults and ability to route logs to your SIEM/KMS.
4) A proposed mutual action plan so we can sequence SOC review, network design, and an initial pilot (we'll attach MAP).

Specific clarification requests for your team: 
- Can you confirm whether the primary requirement is that no user PII leaves your VPC at any time (including ephemeral tokens and KV cache)? Or is filtered/hashed telemetry that excludes direct identifiers acceptable for monitoring?
- Do you have a preferred log retention window (e.g., 30/90/365 days) or a requirement tied to patient-data policies?

Next steps (proposed):
- Aditya and I will update the dataflow with a recommended egress control pattern (we recommend explicit NAT + private endpoints and a VPC egress rule that restricts outbound domains).
- Lauren will surface our answers to smaller audit items like key rotation and KMS integration.
- If you confirm the PII stance, we'll prepare a short statement of capabilities for your procurement and security reviews by next Friday (2026-11-20).

Thanks — I'll wait to hear the PII requirement and preferred log retention timeframe so we can finalize the MAP.

Hi Marissa — thanks for the summary and the quick turnaround on the attachments. A few notes / clarifications from our security and networking side: 

1) PII egress: Our requirement is strict — no raw PII (names, PHI identifiers, patient IDs, or unredacted free text that includes identifiers) may be sent outside our VPC. That includes telemetry that could be reconstituted into identifiers. We can consider hashed or tokenized telemetry if we can agree on the hash scheme and it's irreversible.

2) KV cache: We need assurance that any KV cache used for context does not persist outside our network and that when using Redwood-managed runtime, the KV cache can be mounted on our private subnet or encrypted with keys we control.

3) Logging and retention: Default is 90 days for audit logs, but we may ask for 365 days for certain flows. We also need an option to forward logs (syslog / Splunk / S3) to our ingestion endpoints rather than Redwood retaining them.

4) Egress controls: We prefer a solution where all outbound traffic is forced through our network egress appliance. If Redwood's managed control plane needs to communicate with workers, we'd like that communication to be via private endpoints or via a customer-managed transit.

Would appreciate if Aditya can outline the technical options for KV isolation and private endpoint patterns. Also, is there an option for a self-hosted inference runtime (on-prem) for a pilot?

Sanjay
Director, Platform Security | Acme Health
sanjay.patel@acmehealth.com

Hi Sanjay / team,

Thanks for the clear requirements — wanted to surface concrete options from a technical perspective. TL;DR: we can support a fully private deployment pattern that meets the no-PII-egress requirement; below are trade-offs and implementation notes.

Option A — Redwood Private (VPC peering / PrivateLink + customer-managed KMS):
- Model execution happens on worker nodes within your VPC (dedicated private workers).
- KV cache and ephemeral token memory can be stored on EBS volumes encrypted with keys you control (we support BYOK via KMS/HSM integration).
- Control plane can remain in Redwood's hosted control plane but communicates with workers over AWS PrivateLink (or equivalent) — no public internet egress for inference payloads.
- Logs: we can stream audit logs to your S3/Splunk endpoints; default retention at Redwood can be set to 0 days for PII-sensitive logs.
- Pros: fastest path to production, easier upgrades.
- Cons: requires accepting a private endpoint and some routing setup.

Option B — On-prem / air-gapped package:
- Full package delivered to your environment; no outbound connectivity required.
- All model artifacts and runtime remain on-prem. Updates delivered via secure transfer processes we can contractually define.
- Pros: maximum control for regulated data.
- Cons: longer setup and maintenance.

KV cache specifics:
- We can mount cache stores on volumes in your VPC and rotate encryption keys; for managed workers we can enforce process-level protections to avoid persisting identifiers beyond request lifetime.
- We also support a 'no-persist' mode where ephemeral context is held only in RAM and never written to disk.

Egress patterns / network boundaries:
- Recommend an architecture where all worker outbound calls are blocked by default and only allowed to a small set of private endpoints.
- For control-plane telemetry, we can route health pings over PrivateLink and encrypt traffic with mutual TLS tied to your certs.

Next steps I propose:
1) Lauren and I will prepare a two-page technical brief that maps Option A vs B against your requirements.
2) Marissa / Neha will draft the MAP and proposed timeline.
3) If helpful, we can run a short POC on dedicated private workers configured with 'no-persist' KV mode.

I'll attach a quick reference diagram and will follow with the brief by EOD Monday.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
